lines.en: And so another night ends with me only getting slightly closer to her — but that’s par for the course when her entire life is built around a world that I have no part in.
I stare back at her mansion from the backseat of a ride that I am forced to take and remember just how far apart we are in almost every single way.
And how even in those few moments of feigned intimacy, where our bodies move closer together than they should ever be...that I am an outsider.
I have been one from the start- and there is no way someone like me, who can’t stop plucking his feathers, could ever take a fledgling bird like her under my wing.
For even if I could fly, there is nothing I could show her that she can’t already see from the cage she was brought up in.
After all, it’s miles higher than any of us will ever reach.
You can look up as much you want — but I will hearken back to another recent metaphor involving a hole and reiterate the fact that ascension is far more difficult than its antonym.
She’s the one who will need to come down to us.
But she needs to want it.
And I’m not quite sure if she ever will.
: Arakawa-sama, if you’d be so kind as to inform me of your destination, I would be very grateful. The mistress did not tell me where you were headed tonight.
: I don’t really care, to be honest. You can drop me off wherever.
: I can’t-
: It’s fine, really. I’m not a big fan of cars in the first place.
: I apologize for the inconvenience.
: You may exit the vehicle at your leisure.
The car screeches to a halt in the middle of nowhere and I remove myself from its metal stomach, half-digested from the acid that’s been dripping from my mind as it runs wild once more.
Just, this time, the world alone remains in view.
There is no blackout nor subsequent confusion from an abrupt change in locale.
I can feel my limbs and move my body. I can hear the sounds of the gravel beneath my feet as I walk off in a direction I only half-expect to be the right one.
And all the while, I wish that I was still in her lap.
I wish we could have looked at each other for more than a handful of seconds.
But it’s better that we didn’t.
And it’s better that she’s now with someone who understands her instead of someone who simply wants to.
For a moment, I envision these empty streets as the halls of a lavish manor.
The streetlights are suits of armor. The stars, a chandelier.
And the moon is the face of someone I wish to see — tragically gazing down from a perspective far more interesting than my own.
I’m sure it all looks small to her.
And I’m sure that’s just the way she likes it.
: Hah...I needed this...
: Did you have a long day, dear?
: “Long” doesn’t even begin to describe it. Every second with that man feels like an hour. And the sudden appearance of Tsukasa did not help very much either.
: I’m glad we wound up here instead of the pool. I likely would have drowned from exhaustion if I were to get in there right now.
: I might not be a perfect mother, but even I wouldn’t let my eldest daughter drown right before my very eyes.
: But you would your youngest?
: Oh, stop. You know that’s not what I meant.
: Of course I do.
: But if you just happened to look away for a moment or two, I can’t say I’d blame you.
: Be nice. Tsukasa may be a handful, but she’s dealing with a lot right now.
: Is she? How so?
: It’s no fault of her own. It’s because of me.
: That can’t be true. You haven’t done anything at all.
: I believe that’s...exactly the issue. Tsukasa’s been feeling...left out, I suppose. She isn’t as inherently accepting of my absence as you were at her age.
: Did she...tell you this? That seems rather mature for her.
: Yes and no. There were some...words she shouted at me in the middle of a meeting. But it was Sensei who pointed out the meaning behind all of them as I struggled to wrap my head around it.
: Sensei? You mean...my Sensei? He did that?
: Oh? You’re calling him yours now? Perhaps I was interrupting before, then.
: D...Don’t be ridiculous! It’s excruciatingly obvious that’s not what I meant. I just didn’t think he paid much attention to her at all.
: To think he’d notice something neither of us did despite his limited time with her is...
: Kind of impressive, right?
: I suppose an outsider’s perspective really helps sometimes. I can see now why your sister decided to marry him.
: Guh.
: Would you mind explaining how that came about?
: That...is the unfortunate result of a joke I made in poor taste earlier. Which is precisely why I normally abstain from comedy altogether. It is very much a weakness of mine.
: Did it make you jealous hearing her say that?
: What? Of course not. I just think she should behave around her elders and it irritates me that she’s able to be so...crass. It's as if she doesn’t have a care in the world.
: So you’d accept if she did become his betrothed?
: Mother, just what exactly are you getting at? Why even joke about such a thing?
: Hahah! I suppose I’m just as weak when it comes to comedy as you are.
: I suppose we should just stick to what we do best and let those with less on their plates be the ones to provide the entertainment.
: That said, your teacher really is quite the character, isn’t he?
: Well...yes. But how much time have you been spending with him exactly? Because there are certain...things about him that I can’t imagine you’d brush off as...quirkiness.
: Quite a lot, actually. We’re...partners of sorts. Though, I doubt he’d say the same if you were to ask him.
: I didn’t need to. He came to me.
: Oh?
: I know all about your little scheme to turn my apartment complex into a...re-homing site for the Chosokabe sisters. And I know about Sensei’s involvement in it as well.
: What I wish I knew is why you neglected to provide me the specific details.
: Unless this is just another of your lies. I wouldn’t put it past you, given what you pulled tonight.
: Are you...upset with me?
: No...it’s not that. I agree with everything you’ve done and I understand how...absorbed you become in certain things. I just feel as if I was robbed of a chance to impress you myself.
: Touka, you don’t need to do something like that to impress me. Just...speaking your mind the way you’re doing right now is impressive.
: I think that may be the first time you’ve ever spoken to me like that.
: Ah! Please excuse my temperament! It was not my intention to talk down on you, I just-
: It’s fine. You needn’t apologize. In fact, I wish you’d be honest like that more often.
: It wasn’t my goal to raise you into a woman who just kneels before anyone with more power than her. In fact, the most powerful of all are the ones who fight for what they believe in.
: That is what I want you to be — not a second Tsubasa Tsukioka. Though, I must say, I am quite flattered by just how much of myself I see in you.
: You’re a beautiful young woman, Touka. And I’m sure you’ll be an even more beautiful figurehead one day.
: And while we’re at it, I suppose I should also apologize for sticking my hands where they don’t belong. I simply wanted a better life for Chika and her sister.
: I know...which is why I said I agree with you.
: Additionally, the reason I don’t speak to you in such an...uncouth way more often is that I simply admire everything you do and seldom hear anything I disagree with.
: It just felt a little bit like you didn’t trust me this time. That’s all.
: That’s not it at all, dear. I tried to involve you as much as I could. There are just certain aspects of Sensei’s involvement that would best be kept under wraps.
: I likely know about those as well.
: You...do?
: Sensei explained the whole situation to me. How his relationship with Chika is not...of the normal student-teacher variety.
: He openly told you that?! Are you sure you didn’t just...discern this information on your own?
: He omitted some of the details, but...it was quite obvious what he was trying to say.
: Ugh. Just when I was beginning to believe I understood him. What a confusing man he is.
: The bright side to all of this, though, is that it means he trusts you. And that’s something that can be leveraged.
: Leveraged?...
: Not for anything improper, of course. It’s just information you can use to plot out your next action.
: My next...what? I’m not sure what you mean by that.
: Am I to take over the responsibilities of relocating the Chosokabe family in your stead?
: Of course not. I’m not trying to create more work for you when your schedule is already busy enough.
: I simply mean that knowing he trusts you will make it easier for the two of you to sleep together.
: Can you please repeat that? I think there may be water in my ears.
: You do want to sleep with him, don’t you?
: What?! Why?!....What?!
: There’s no need to yell, dear. You’re at the age where it’s completely natural to be thinking about things like that.
: Plus, it was written all over your face earlier. In fact, it’s written on there now as well.
: Have you gone mad?! What is happening right now?!
: We’re bonding! Oh, it’s been so long since I’ve been able to engage in “girl talk” with anyone. And seeing as I’m your mother, there's no need to shy away from touchy subjects like intercourse.
: Do you have any questions for me? I’d be happy to help.
: Only about a million or so.
: Well, let’s start with one and see how things go from there. Shoot.
: Shoot.
: Touka, there’s absolutely nothing wrong with feeling the way you feel. Well, at least not from your perspective.
: Your body is going through changes and-
: I have seen more than enough “instructional videos” to know precisely what “changes” my body is going through, Mother.
: What I do not see is why you’d insinuate and seemingly endorse me doing something like that with my teacher when I’m still this...young.
: Because we’re in a position fortunate enough to do anything we want whenever it is we want to do it.
: And if there is something you want, even if you are not supposed to have it, I don’t mind if you try to reach out and grab it.
: “It” in this case, of course, being your teacher. Will you at least admit that the thought has crossed your mind?
: Touka, it’s fine. I will understand.
: Of...course it’s crossed my mind. As you said, thinking about such things at my age is completely normal. I am aware of that.
: Then what is it that’s preventing you from moving forward? The consequences? The...risk? What is it?
: The...everything.
: I won’t deny that I...often find myself gravitating toward him in many more ways than I ever expected to, but I don’t believe we’re anywhere near the level required to do something like that yet.
: Level?
: What I mean is...we’re not in love.
: I’ve seen the way he acts with some of the other girls in class, and you can feel a connection between those pairs that he and I distinctly lack.
: Who am I to take what I want when I haven’t worked nearly as hard for it as they have?
: Touka, a key benefit to being who we are is not having to work as hard as others.
: Besides, there’s no need for a connection of that level when you can simply just use him to satisfy the...cravings you may have. Any man in their right mind would jump for joy at a deal like that.
: Who are you and what have you done with my perfect mother?!
: Perfection is just a mask we put on to impress those around us. When that mask comes off, we’re all the same, Touka.

: I’m not endorsing the idea of you going around and sleeping with all of the remaining men in Kumon-mi. I’m just saying I trust your judgement and wouldn’t blame you for indulging those desires of yours.
: It doesn’t even have to be Sensei if you’re dead set on being “in love” with him first. We have an entire massage staff who would be more than happy to assist you.
: How do you think I stayed sane when I was your age?
: Mother!
: Ahh...how I miss those days. Things are no fun anymore now that I’m unable to let my guard down.
: But it doesn’t have to be that way for you. You can-
: Oh, no. Don’t you go admitting something like that and then giving me a motivational speech about why it’s okay to abuse the massage staff.
: Abuse? I’d never make them do anything they didn’t already want to. And if it weren’t for my mother, I never would have known about those services in the first place.
: This goes back generations and generations, Touka. It’s not a new thing.
: This tradition...ends with me.
: Why? It’s completely natural and really helps take the edge off. If you think this bath is relaxing, just imagine how-
: Mother.
: I do not want to talk to you right now.
: Fine. Two can play at that game. But don’t come crying to me when your urges become too much for you to bear.
: As my mother, you would be the last person I’d ever come to for that in the first place.
: Hmph!
: Hmph!
: This was fun. We should spend time together like this more often.
: I agree. Looking past the many things I learned about you tonight, it was very nice getting to speak to you in a way much...different than normal.
: And I mean much different. I wasn’t even aware this side of you existed.
: What do you say to having our next get-together in the massage lounge?
: I say that I am suddenly tired and have decided to retire for the night.
: Goodnight, Mother. If that is really who you are.
: It’s who I’ve always been, dear. I just think you’re mature enough to hear about it now.
: I’m barely a freshman!
I peel off my shirt, now drenched with cum from battling loneliness, and toss it across the room into a pile of others that have met the same fate.
You’d never guess who I thought of tonight.
I hope she thought the same of me.
And I hope her clothes are lying in a pile right now.
She did.
And they were.
Touka’s affection has increased to [touka_love]!
